The window is confounded under D-133, and three setup sub-makes bypassed the admission wrapper; both are disclosed. `publisherTrace32`'s comment now describes D-154. 4 commits, 115 owned files. | w1-netlab follow-up 35 | F22-01's diagnosis and new TCP evidence (`docs/poc/G2-followup35-2026-11-04.md`). The agent has no positive minimum Apply spacing: binding-deadline wake-ups, a zero remaining Step delay and a closed recovery's second Apply in the same Step can all apply within 400 ms. So D-159's condition is false, and the campaign's cadence is unchanged. Measured retry offsets (+208, +416 and +826 ms), transplanted onto F22-01's and F27-01/B1's sends, meet later install brackets: timing-compatible, not proven, since neither run retained TCP packets. The three collectors now keep combined TCP/UDP headers with absolute sequence numbers and their original counters; a checked projection feeds the byte-identical D-120 analyzer, and the stream records each TCP echo as match, EOF, stale or mismatch. Five standalone attempts: the first failed on the new splitter and stays failed (fixed, with a regression test); four passed with zero TCP timeouts and a TCP p95 of 205 to 209 ms; attempts 3 to 5 conservatively confounded. In attempt 3, sequence 47 entered the node twice inside generations 1069 and 1070's install brackets before a 613 ms read. The full netlab gate and all 13 agent scenarios pass. Historical failures stay failed. 7 commits, 397 owned files, mostly evidence. Session on codex gpt-6-astra. | done (#462) |

| w2-updater follow-up 25 | F30-01's update-good exit 3, diagnosed and addressed under D-158 as revised (`docs/updates/node-followup25-2026-11-04.md`). Ordinary agent Apply contention is the supported explanation: the agent's hold is bounded by its Step's local deadline, about 10 s, not by the sampled half-second, so the brief's 2 s bound was not supported and the lane stopped; the orchestrator revised D-158. Now `run`, `seed`, `apply` and standalone `flush` wait for a live `update.lock` holder within one 10 s budget, polling every 20 ms; past it they exit 3 with the unchanged `UPDATE_BUSY: lock` line. `recover` and standalone `Retain` keep five attempts 20 ms apart; nested calls reuse ownership; stale details keep exit 1 after five attempts counted from the first stale answer; unreadable metadata stays busy; cancellation ends the wait. One JSON record, `update lock wait` with command, waited_ms, acquired and budget_ms, only after a missed first attempt; an uncontended command's stderr is unchanged. Proofs with a real second holder: a 600 ms holder gave exit 3 at about 81 ms before the change and exit 0 at about 617 ms after it, for all four commands; the CLI's real default budget exits 3 at 10.006 s. Common lock APIs, the exit table and the agent, installer and update AT consumers are unchanged. F30-01 stays open until an acceptance run reaches the candidate. 8 commits, 9 owned files. Session on codex gpt-6-astra, with one resume. | done (#463) |
